Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we’re a small lighting crew at the bellwether playhouse and need help turning these notes into a practical incident review and plan for our next focus rehearsal. please keep it specific to this show and our room, not a general guide to theatre electrics. the show is the winter guest, a new play in the 118-seat studio. our crew is me, mara, who is the lighting supervisor, dev, our programmer, and jo, a volunteer who can work two evenings a week. the director is elian price. we have one focus rehearsal booked for thursday 6 to 10 pm, and the first invited audience is friday at 7:30. nobody is asking for a report on the artistic choices in the script.

on monday we noticed that the practical lamp on the kitchen table flickered during scene four. it uses a dimmable led bulb supplied by the set designer, not a lamp from our normal stock. mara saw it flicker twice when the channel was at 38 percent, but it stayed steady at full. dev wrote down that the lamp was plugged into outlet b-3 through a short black extension. we haven’t tested a replacement bulb yet, and we don’t know whether the flicker comes from the bulb, the dimmer, or the extension. please keep those possibilities open rather than treating one as confirmed. the designer, rafi, said, “that bulb was fine in the shop, but i can bring the spare on thursday.” he has not promised to arrive before the call starts.

there is another issue at the back wall. when the actors cross from the doorway to the bench, the floor is very dark for roughly two steps. it was easiest to see during the run when the work light was off and the blue wash was at 22 percent. elian asked us after the run, “can we see the crossing without making the doorway look like a new scene?” that is a request, not a direction to raise the whole wash. the doorway is on a separate cue, and we need to keep the end of scene three visually distinct from the start of scene four. jo can mark the crossing with tape before thursday, but the tape must come off before the invited audience enters.

our equipment and room limit what we can try. the console is an etc element 2, and the stage has six led pars, four fresnels and two profile fixtures available for this show. all twelve are already patched, but we have one spare dimmer channel and no spare led fixture. the house electrician has asked us not to move the ladder onto the audience-side aisle because the handrail there is loose. we can use the short platform from the scene shop, though it takes two people to carry it. the booth has a printed plot from the start of the week; dev has changed two channel labels since then but has not reprinted it. there is no extra rehearsal time available on friday, and the actors are called at 6:15 thursday, so any tests that need an empty stage should happen before then.

what i’d like is a short incident review followed by a usable plan for the four-hour focus call. please identify what we know, what is still uncertain, and what we should check, without claiming that a test has happened. put the evidence before any recommendations. for the recommendations, use a numbered checklist in rehearsal order; that numbered format applies to the recommended actions only, not to the evidence or the review. include who could take each action when the notes identify someone, and flag anything that needs confirmation rather than assigning it as settled. we need something the three of us can read at the booth, not a formal report for the board.

there are a couple of timing and safety details that matter to the plan. if rafi brings the spare bulb before 6 pm, we can compare it with the current bulb before the actors arrive; if he does not, we should still be able to test the existing lamp and record what happens, without assuming the spare is available. any work near the back wall should use the scene-shop platform with two people, not the audience-side aisle ladder. we also need to leave the stage ready for the actors by 6:15, and jo’s crossing tape needs to be removed before the invited audience comes in friday. please carry those conditions through the relevant steps, but don’t invent an extra call, extra equipment, or an answer to the flicker.

finally, please keep the output grounded in these notes and distinguish direct observations from guesses and requests. include the practical lamp, the dark crossing, the separate doorway cue, the patch and fixture limits, the outdated printed plot, the loose handrail, and the actual rehearsal and audience times. we need the last part to address what remains unresolved after the thursday call, including the possibility that the bulb is not the cause and the fact that friday has no added test time. end with that remaining-work paragraph; don’t add a general conclusion or a claim that the plan has fixed anything.", "output": "Create a concise, booth-friendly incident review and rehearsal plan for the lighting crew at the Bellwether Playhouse, based only on the notes below. Keep the review specific to *The Winter Guest* in the 118-seat studio; do not turn it into a general guide to theatre electrics or a formal report for the board. Do not assess the script’s artistic choices, claim that any test has already happened, or present an uncertain cause as confirmed.

The crew is Mara, the lighting supervisor; Dev, the programmer; and Jo, a volunteer available two evenings a week. The director is Elian Price. The next focus rehearsal is Thursday, 6–10 pm, and the first invited audience is Friday at 7:30 pm. Actors are called Thursday at 6:15 pm, so any test requiring an empty stage must happen before then. There is no additional rehearsal or test time on Friday.

Organize the review around the following two issues:

- **Practical lamp in scene four:** On Monday, Mara saw the kitchen-table practical flicker twice at channel level 38 percent and remain steady at full. Dev noted that it was plugged into outlet B-3 through a short black extension. It uses a dimmable LED bulb supplied by set designer Rafi, rather than a lamp from the crew’s usual stock. No replacement bulb has been tested. Keep the bulb, dimmer, and extension as possible causes; the notes do not establish which, if any, is responsible. Rafi said, “that bulb was fine in the shop, but i can bring the spare on thursday.” He has not promised to arrive before the call.
- **Dark crossing at the back wall:** Actors crossing from the doorway to the bench have roughly two steps of very dark floor. The issue was easiest to see during the run with the work light off and blue wash at 22 percent. Elian asked, “can we see the crossing without making the doorway look like a new scene?” Treat this as a request, not an instruction to raise the whole wash. The doorway has a separate cue, and the end of scene three must remain visually distinct from the start of scene four. Jo can mark the crossing with tape before Thursday; the tape must be removed before the invited audience enters Friday.

Use the available equipment and safety information accurately. The console is an ETC Element 2. The show has six LED pars, four fresnels, and two profile fixtures; all twelve are patched. There is one spare dimmer channel but no spare LED fixture. The printed plot in the booth is from the start of the week. Dev has since changed two channel labels but has not reprinted it. The house electrician has asked the crew not to put the ladder on the audience-side aisle because its handrail is loose. Work near the back wall must use the short scene-shop platform, carried by two people. Do not propose equipment, access, or rehearsal time that the notes say is unavailable.

Write a short incident review that separates direct observations, outstanding uncertainties, and requests. Put the evidence before any recommendations. Then give a usable plan for the four-hour Thursday focus call. Present **recommended actions only** as a numbered checklist in rehearsal order; do not number the evidence or review. Include a responsible person where the notes identify one, and mark assignments or arrangements needing confirmation rather than treating them as settled. Keep the plan readable at the booth.

Carry the timing and safety conditions through the relevant checklist steps. If Rafi brings the spare bulb before 6 pm, the crew can compare it with the current bulb before the actors arrive. If he does not, the crew should still be able to test the existing lamp and record what happens, without assuming the spare is available. Any work near the back wall must use the scene-shop platform with two people, never the audience-side aisle ladder. Leave the stage ready for the actors by 6:15 pm. Ensure Jo’s crossing tape is removed before the invited audience enters Friday. Do not invent another call, additional equipment, a test result, or a resolution to the flicker.

End with a substantive paragraph identifying what remains unresolved after Thursday’s call. Include that the bulb may not be the cause and that Friday has no added test time. Keep the practical lamp, dark crossing, separate doorway cue, equipment and patch limits, outdated printed plot, loose handrail, and actual rehearsal and audience times in view. Distinguish observations from guesses and requests throughout, and do not append a general conclusion or claim that the plan has fixed anything."}]
